P1.evidence: No setter code and no application referenced, so the read-back does not apply. The usual three-part frame: 'It's just an opportunity for me to understand where you are. Where are you today? Where do you want to be? If we can help, I can show you some options.' No 'what's in the way' element, and agreement was the trailing 'Okay' answered 'Okay'. The open question ran cleanly: 'How could we potentially help you?'

P2.evidence: The second-best Baseline in this folder and the rep announced it: 'Let's get a further baseline for yourself before we dive in a bit further.' Height and weight were actively confirmed ('You said you're six foot and a half and 185, correct?') and age was on record at 60. The training week was elicited properly — 'Monday to Sunday, what's your typical training regimen at the moment?' Sleep was asked directly and worked well: 'And how is your sleep? Are you waking up rested?' produced the 9.30 bedtime, the seven hours, the bladder waking and the scrolling habit. Energy was the best-explored item on the call, pursued across several turns through the 2 p.m. crash, the 5.30 starts and the Red Bull history. What is missing is everything clinical and everything dietary. No health or medication question was asked, so the statin, the reflux medication, the testosterone conversation with his urologist and above all the vestibular disorder all arrived unprompted. The injury check scores a partial only because 'What makes you say that? Why don't you want to do that?' happened to draw out the elbow story; it was not an injury question. Diet was never asked, despite the prospect volunteering that his eating collapsed into takeaways when his daughter moved out.

P3.evidence: The mirror image of the usual shape in this folder: the surface ran and the depth did not. The metric question was good — 'what is the single biggest metric that you're hoping to really improve here? Is it the vitality overall? Is it losing some body fat, gaining some muscle?' — and produced 'I just want to feel fit. I want to feel stronger.' The bridge was attempted twice and failed both times: 'in which arenas in your life do you want to feel the boost in fitness and strength?' got 'I just want to feel good all the time', and the rephrase — 'Where in your life, your day-to-day, your routine, do you not feel as fit or as strong?' — got a defensive answer about riding an 850cc motorcycle. After two attempts the rep abandoned the thread. The two checks that would have opened it were never asked. 'Who else does that impact' was never put, despite a daughter who has moved out, a dog he feels obligated to, and an explicit longevity fear. The prospect eventually supplied the answer himself, unprompted, at 00:21:42: 'Being there for my family, being there for my pet, you know, I also have to be there for myself.' That sentence was available twenty minutes earlier for the asking.

P4.evidence: Complete and well run. Past attempts were fully mapped — the fifteen-year basement gym, Arizona, boxing, the Rogue pull-up and dip bars during COVID, the current $300/mo membership — and what happened to each was drawn out. The blocker question was direct: 'What is stopping you from doing that then?' and it produced the real answer about mornings, rushing and post-work exhaustion. The prospect named his own gap without being led: 'It's discipline' and 'Maybe I just need a template. Maybe I just need some motivation. Maybe I just need somebody to say get off your arse.' The self-sufficiency challenge ran almost verbatim — 'Because we live in the digital age, right? Information is so abundant. ChatGPT, Claude, YouTube, I can go on and on' — followed by 'what is the rationale when it comes to getting outside help as opposed to doing it yourself?' A textbook run of this phase.

P5.evidence: Effectively absent. No two-year question, no cost of inaction, no why-not, no line in the sand. The one move in the right register was 'You're fit and strong for someone your age range... Why not just continue as you are?', which is a settle-for challenge in substance, but it was asked once and not followed up, and the answer — 'Well, that's my goal' — went unchallenged. This is the phase that decided the call. The prospect had handed over the raw material for a genuinely powerful consequence frame: he is 60, he is a doctor who knows exactly what sarcopenia does, and he said out loud 'I don't want to be like these brittle old people who can barely walk.' Nothing was built on it. Without a consequence, the rep concluded there was no need and disqualified — but the need was never tested, only observed.

P6.evidence: Not attempted in any form. No trust gauge, no capability check, no all-in question. The rep moved from Phase 4 straight to 'would you like me to be honest with you or nice?' and disqualified. Marked as misses rather than not applicable because the phase was reachable and the rep chose not to run it: a commitment check is exactly the instrument that would have told him whether the low urgency he was reading was real or simply unexcavated, and it would have cost ninety seconds.

P11.evidence: The rep disqualified the prospect from the coaching programme and never quoted a coaching price, so payment, the Trevor booking, the agreement and onboarding were all unreachable. A Primal University link was placed in the Zoom chat and the prospect declined to enrol on the call.

objection_plays.detail: SCRIPT GAP AND THE DEFINING ISSUE OF THIS CALL — there is no scripted procedure for qualifying a prospect out. Three calls in this batch end in the rep deciding the prospect does not need the product, and each time he improvises the same ad-hoc device: 'would you like me to be honest with you or nice?' followed by a personal judgement. The playbook has plays for prospects who resist and nothing at all for prospects the rep concludes are self-sufficient. That matters commercially here, because on the ICP as the company itself states it this is the single best-qualified prospect in the folder — a practising physician, good money, health as the neglected area, good-to-great, visibly not deconditioned — and he was disqualified on a criterion that appears nowhere in the ICP, on the basis of a Consequence Frame that was never run.

SCRIPT GAP — 'a cheap alternative already worked for me', third instance in this batch and the most concrete version yet. He named the vendor, the items, the prices and the result: 'Rogue Fitness. 130 bucks, I got an incredible pull-up bar, 120 bucks, I got like a dip bar... and I just did pull-ups and dips, and I stayed in great shape.' Roughly $250 of equipment, six years ago, and it worked. The rep did not engage with it at all, moving instead to a question about apartment space. This is the gap already logged in playbook.json against the Badrane Hriouch call, now recurring across three prospects in one folder.

SCRIPT GAP — the environmental blocker. His constraint is not motivation, money or knowledge; it is that he moved from a house with a fully equipped basement gym to an apartment with a mat in a spare bedroom, and he gets no psychological 'charge' from training at home. He said it twice: 'I really get a charge out of going to the gym' and 'I'll do kettlebell at the gym and get more of a charge out of it than doing it in my little third bedroom here.' Since the entire product is a home-based programme, this is a direct objection to the delivery model and there is nothing scripted for it. Recommending an unsupervised home video programme to a man who has just explained that home training does not engage him is the predictable result.

'No, I want to take a look at it... I need to see.' No play ran; the rep accepted immediately with 'Sure. Any questions that you need me to answer?' Recorded for completeness rather than as a criticism — this was a deferral on a $200 subscription after the rep had already disqualified him from the main product, and pressing would have contradicted the position he had just taken.

notes: Phase 4 is textbook and Baseline is the second-strongest in this folder, including the only proper sleep question in the batch. The call was decided by what did not run. With no Consequence Frame and no commitment check, the rep read low urgency as low need and disqualified the best-qualified prospect in the folder — a 60-year-old physician who told him plainly that he fears ending up unable to walk. The single highest-value coaching point is sequencing: run Phase 5 before forming a judgement about need, because urgency that has not been excavated is not the same as urgency that does not exist. Second point, and separate: two attempts at the bridge question in the same phrasing is not enough, and 'who else does that impact' was never asked of a man with a daughter, a dog and a stated fear of frailty.
